title: Fibre Euler characteristic of a flat finitely presented sheaf in a proper family
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a proper morphism of finite presentation of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $\mathcal F$ be an $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], flat over $S$: for every $x\in X$, the stalk $\mathcal F_x$ is flat as an $\mathcal O_{S,f(x)}$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. For $s\in S$, set $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ and $\mathcal F_s=\mathcal F|_{X_s}$, where restriction denotes module pullback [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-fibre-product, def-pc-module-pullback]. Then the integer-valued function $s\mapsto\chi(X_s,\mathcal F_s)$ [def-pc-euler-characteristic] is locally constant: every point of $S$ has an open neighbourhood on which this function is constant. For any morphism $g:S'\to S$, put $X'=X\times_SS'$, let $g':X'\to X$ be the projection, and put $\mathcal F'=g'^*\mathcal F$. For every $s'\in S'$ one has $\chi(X'_{s'},\mathcal F'_{s'})=\chi(X_{g(s')},\mathcal F_{g(s')})$. No Noetherian or reducedness hypothesis on $S$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0B9T, lemma-chi-locally-constant-geometric, statement and base-change clause, lines 7961--7972.

proof.text: Fix $t\in S$. Apply [lem-pc-universal-finite-free-complex] to $f$ and $\mathcal F$: its hypotheses are exactly properness and finite presentation of $f$, finite presentation of $\mathcal F$, and flatness of $\mathcal F$ over $S$ (flatness of $f$ is not required). Obtain an open $V\ni t$, a complex $P$ supported in $[0,d]$, and finite ranks $r_i$ with $P^i\cong\mathcal O_V^{r_i}$. Keep its comparison for every cartesian base change along every map to $V$. Only existence of the cohomology isomorphisms is needed, not their canonicity or functoriality.

source.place: Tag 0B9T, lemma-chi-locally-constant-geometric, proof; local finite-free computation in Tag 0BDJ, lemma-chi-locally-constant, proof.

proof.text: Let $L$ be any field and $a:\operatorname{Spec}L\to V$ any morphism. Put $Y=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}L$ and let $\mathcal G$ be the pullback of $\mathcal F$. By [lem-pc-universal-finite-free-complex], $H^i(a^*P)\cong R^i(Y\to\operatorname{Spec}L)_*\mathcal G$. The Zariski space $\operatorname{Spec}L$ has one point: a module sheaf is just its $L$-vector space of sections, so taking sections preserves kernels and quotients. Thus these are isomorphisms of cohomology vector spaces. By the tensor formula in [def-pc-module-pullback], the resulting complex $C$ has $C^i=L^{r_i}$ and is zero outside $[0,d]$. Set $b_i=\dim_L\operatorname{im}(d_C^i)$, with $b_{-1}=b_d=0$. Rank-nullity gives $\dim\ker(d_C^i)=r_i-b_i$, and quotienting by $\operatorname{im}(d_C^{i-1})\subseteq\ker(d_C^i)$ gives $\dim H^i(C)=r_i-b_i-b_{i-1}$. All these dimensions are finite and the cohomology vanishes outside $[0,d]$. In the alternating sum the $b_i$ terms cancel in consecutive degrees, including the zero boundary terms. By [def-pc-euler-characteristic], therefore $\chi(Y,\mathcal G)=\sum_{i=0}^d(-1)^i r_i$. This calculation uses no hypothesis on $L$ or on the map $a$.

source.place: Tag 0B9T, lemma-chi-locally-constant-geometric, proof; local finite-free computation in Tag 0BDJ, lemma-chi-locally-constant, proof.

proof.text: For each $s\in V$, take $L=\kappa(s)$ and $a:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to V$ the canonical morphism. The calculation in step 2 gives $\chi(X_s,\mathcal F_s)=\sum_{i=0}^d(-1)^i r_i$, independent of $s$. Thus the function is constant on the open neighbourhood $V$ of $t$. Since $t$ was arbitrary, it is locally constant.

source.place: Tag 0B9T, lemma-chi-locally-constant-geometric, proof; local finite-free computation in Tag 0BDJ, lemma-chi-locally-constant, proof.

proof.text: Now let $g:S^{\prime}\to S$ and $s^{\prime}\in S^{\prime}$, and choose the model of step 1 at $t=g(s^{\prime})$. The composite $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s^{\prime})\to S^{\prime}\to S$ factors through $V$, since its one-point image is $t\in V$; denote this factor by $a$. The universal property in [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $(X\times_S S^{\prime})\times_{S^{\prime}}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s^{\prime})$ with $X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s^{\prime})$: maps into either side are exactly compatible maps into $X$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s^{\prime})$. The composite-pullback isomorphism in [def-pc-module-pullback] identifies $\mathcal F^{\prime}_{s^{\prime}}$ with the pullback of $\mathcal F$ in this square. Apply the universal comparison of [lem-pc-universal-finite-free-complex] to this map $a$. The calculation of step 2 gives $\chi(X^{\prime}_{s^{\prime}},\mathcal F^{\prime}_{s^{\prime}})=\sum_{i=0}^d(-1)^i r_i$, which equals $\chi(X_t,\mathcal F_t)$ by step 3. This proves the asserted pointwise equality for every base change. Neither the local model nor the calculation imposed Noetherianity or reducedness on $S$.

theorem isLocallyConstant_eulerCharFiber (hℱ : ℱ.IsFlatOver f) :
    IsLocallyConstant (ℱ.eulerCharFiber f)
lean.note: Existing upstream statements jointly give both clauses of Stacks 0B9T. The main declaration states local constancy for a finitely presented module flat over a proper locally finitely presented morphism. QuasiCompact follows from properness, and injective resolutions exist for every scheme module category by isGrothendieckAbelian. The second declaration gives the pointwise equality for every cartesian base-change square; specialize to pullback.fst and pullback.snd. It already holds without the flatness and local-finite-presentation hypotheses, so applies to all the objects of this node. IsFlatOver is the affine-local equivalent of stalkwise relative flatness for this quasi-coherent module. No new module or definition is needed.
